passage:
Lena's watch stopped at 3:17. She planned to throw it away, but her brother said it looked nice and asked to keep it.
He wore it even though it did not tell time. His friends asked why.
He said, "It reminds me that time is not only numbers."
Lena thought this was silly until she learned that 3:17 was the time their family had arrived at their new home years ago. Their mother had written it in an old diary.
The stopped watch became meaningful by accident.
It no longer measured passing time, but it marked one important moment. Sometimes an object stops working as a tool and starts working as a memory.
